skill.name: mirrord-operator
skill.description: Help users install and configure the mirrord Operator for team/enterprise environments. Use when users ask about operator setup, Helm installation, cloud API key or license configuration, air-gapped/offline licensing, enabling features (queue splitting, DB branching, preview environments, multi-cluster), internal registries, OpenShift/GKE Autopilot, RBAC, or multi-user mirrord deployments. Also use when an AI agent hits a Team or Enterprise feature on a cluster with no license and needs to offer the user a trial (agent-started trial; the trial is Enterprise tier).
skill.summary: Guide mirrord Operator installation, licensing, feature configuration, and troubleshooting for Kubernetes teams.
skill.author: metalbear-co

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting, YAML comments, and legitimate configuration references. Confirmed risks involve inline credentials, trial response exposure, and HTTP licensing; additional findings address transport security, database authentication, and excessive permissions. No evidence found of prompt injection or malicious intent; cluster changes and trial registration explicitly require user approval.

remediation.issue: Inline authentication examples conflict with the stated secret-handling rules.
remediation.suggestion: Remove inline API key, license key, and license PEM examples from operational guidance. Use Kubernetes Secret or Google Secret Manager references consistently.

remediation.issue: The trial signup command prints a response containing an API key.
remediation.suggestion: Capture the response in a permission-restricted temporary file outside agent output. Parse it locally, transfer credentials securely, redact displayed fields, and remove temporary data.

remediation.issue: Self-hosted license server examples use HTTP for shared-secret authentication.
remediation.suggestion: Use HTTPS with a trusted certificate, or explicitly require an authenticated encrypted transport before sharing the license key.

remediation.issue: API service certificate verification and agent transport encryption are disabled in the supplied defaults.
remediation.suggestion: Document a production override enabling agent TLS and API service certificate verification. Provision trusted certificates and verify connectivity before rollout.

remediation.issue: IAM-backed PostgreSQL branches are documented to accept arbitrary credentials by default.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend password authentication for IAM-backed branches and restrict network access to authorized workloads. Explain the trust-mode exposure before enabling branching.

remediation.issue: Literal database credentials enable cluster-wide Secret permissions by default.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend disabling dbBranchingLiteralCredentials unless required. Use existing Secret references and review rendered RBAC permissions before installation.

content.user_title: Configure mirrord Operator for Kubernetes Teams
content.value_statement: Team deployments require coordinated licensing, Kubernetes permissions, and feature configuration. This skill guides mirrord Operator setup and troubleshooting with Helm references and approval checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Guide Helm installation, upgrades, removal, and operator status checks.
Explain cloud API key, Kubernetes Secret, Google Secret Manager, and offline licensing options.
Identify Helm flags for queue splitting, database branching, preview environments, and multi-cluster operation.
Provide configuration guidance for internal registries, OpenShift, GKE Autopilot, TLS, and chart-provided RBAC roles.
Troubleshoot authentication failures, unavailable operators, certificate errors, resource limits, and interrupted sessions.
Guide Enterprise trial registration after explicit approval and explain organization ownership requirements.
limitations: Execution requires installed Kubernetes, Helm, and mirrord tooling with appropriate cluster permissions.
Team features require licensing; offline deployments require Enterprise licensing rather than the connected trial.
Feature compatibility depends on operator, chart, and client versions; some detailed workflows reference separate skills.
The skill provides guidance, not a security guarantee; credential examples and transport defaults require review before production use.

output: Use an Enterprise offline license certificate or a self-hosted license server.

best_practices: Confirm cluster context, namespaces, exact commands, and user approval before every cluster modification.
Use Secret references, protect temporary credential files, and keep API keys out of agent output and committed values.
Enable only required features, restrict access and branch images, and review TLS settings before production deployment.
anti_patterns: Pasting authentication secrets into chat, command arguments, or committed Helm values.
Starting trials or changing shared clusters without explicit user approval.
Enabling preview environments or generic branching without reviewing permissions, image restrictions, and network access.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill include the mirrord Operator?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions and reference values. Installation uses the external Helm chart and requires cluster access.

faq.question: Can I use it without an existing license?
faq.answer: The skill describes a seven-day Enterprise trial with explicit approval. Registration creates an external organization that the user must claim.

faq.question: Does the trial work in an air-gapped cluster?
faq.answer: No. The documented trial requires telemetry connectivity. Offline deployments use Enterprise license certificates or a self-hosted license server.

faq.question: Should I give the agent my API key?
faq.answer: No. Create the credential Secret yourself and provide its reference. Keep secret values out of chat, logs, and committed configuration.

faq.question: Will installation enable every feature?
faq.answer: No. Most advanced features require separate Helm flags and compatible versions. Enable only requested features after reviewing their permissions and security implications.
